claims.statement: The Client Secret is a confidential key generated by Zoom and assigned to a Zoom app; a newly generated secret leaves the previous one working for 30 days unless it is revoked sooner with the rotate client secret API.

sources.supports: Client Secret is a confidential key generated by Zoom and assigned to your Zoom app.
Your current secret will continue to work for 30 days after a new secret is generated.

claims.statement: Zoom's OAuth reference says token requests to https://zoom.us/oauth/token (authorization code exchange and refresh for General apps) carry a Basic Authorization header, which is the Client ID and Client Secret joined by a colon and Base64 encoded; PKCE with a public client ID needs no client secret.

sources.supports: The Basic Authorization header is your Client ID and Client Secret by a colon (:) and Base64 encoded. Use PKCE to enable user authorization with a public client ID an no client secret, without the need for a backend server.
sources.locator: Request an access token, App Type: General, Exchange authorization code for access token

sources.supports: To refresh an access token, send a POST request to https://zoom.us/oauth/token with a basic authorization header. ... The basic authorization header is your Client ID and Client Secret with a colon : in between, Base64 Encoded.
sources.locator: Refresh an access token, App Type: General

claims.statement: Zoom's app credentials page shows the client secret as a client_secret form field (with client_id) in an example authorization code token request made with development credentials; this differs from the Basic header form of the OAuth reference.

sources.supports: When setting up OAuth for user authorization, the development client ID and client secret are used to generate access tokens. (example POST https://zoom.us/oauth/token, x-www-form-urlencoded, with grant_type, code, redirect_uri, client_id and client_secret fields)
sources.locator: Credentials in Development vs Production, When to use development credentials, Testing OAuth authentication

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Draft; not yet reviewed.

openQuestions.question: Not researched beyond existence: prefix, alphabet, length and any checksum are not stated on the pages read, and no value shape may be inferred from the examples (docs examples are placeholders or illustrative).
The page distinguishes production and development credentials (separate client IDs and secrets); whether they differ in shape is not stated.

The Public Key (bring your own key) alternative to a client secret is described only as a choice on the page read; it is a key the developer supplies, not a Zoom-issued string, and is not a candidate.

The OAuth reference describes the Basic header form; the app credentials page shows a client_secret form field only in a development-credentials example. Which form the token endpoint accepts for production credentials beyond the Basic header form was not established; both are recorded as stated.
The Basic envelope encodes the secret together with the public client ID; no prefix, alphabet or width of the secret is stated and the example Basic values are placeholders, not a format.
